issues.title: Coalesce sparse filtered scan chunks before emitting
issues.hypothesis: After a selective table filter or join BF, the table scan emits one DataChunk per 2048-row storage vector, even when only a few rows pass. Every operator downstream then pays its fixed per-chunk overhead on tiny chunks. Hot evidence: in q08 (127ms, 0.77s CPU), HASH_JOIN l_partkey=p_partkey takes 0.405s CPU (52% of the query) for only 403K probe rows. Those rows arrive as about 29K chunks of about 14 rows each, because the exact BF from part passes 0.67% of lineitem's 60M rows. Isolated micro `SELECT count(*) FROM lineitem, part WHERE p_partkey=l_partkey AND p_type='PROMO BURNISHED TIN'`: HJ 0.112s for 403K sparse probe rows, which is 277ns/row. The same join with join_filter_pushdown disabled and dense input (l_orderkey<1600000, 1.6M probe rows) takes 0.039s, which is 25ns/row. That leaves about 3.5us of fixed cost per chunk (the probe key executor, Probe/ScanStructure init, two ExecuteInternal calls per chunk, CachingOperator, and the sink downstream). If the scan fills output chunks to at least about 1K rows, that per-chunk cost is paid about 70x fewer times. Note: memory.md lists 'compacting sparse scan chunks' as refuted, but there is no ledger record of it. This measurement is new, direct evidence that the cost is per chunk and not per row.
issues.plan: In src/function/table/table_scan.cpp, DuckTableScanState::TableScanFunc (~line 316): after storage.Scan returns a non-empty chunk with output.size() < COALESCE_MIN (e.g. STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE/4 = 512), and the scan is not is_create_index, keep calling storage.Scan into a per-local-state scratch DataChunk (TableScanLocalState, initialized with the output types). Stop when the accumulated size reaches the target, or when storage.Scan returns 0 rows (the assigned parallel range is exhausted, so the batch/row-group boundary and batch index are preserved). Append each scratch result into output with DataChunk::Append, which flattens dictionary/FSST/constant vectors. Only the few selected rows get copied, so decoding them is cheap. If a scratch chunk would overflow STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE, keep it as a pending chunk in local state and emit it first on the next call (output.Reference/Move or Append into the empty output). Handle both the CanRemoveFilterColumns path (scan into all_columns, then ReferenceColumns projection_ids; coalesce after projection, or coalesce all_columns before projecting) and the direct path. Only coalesce when the scan has table filters or dynamic filters (input.filters non-empty), so unfiltered scans stay zero-copy. Do not advance NextParallelScan inside the coalesce loop. Verify on q08 that HJ l_partkey time drops in the JSON profile, and check q13 (FSST orders scan with NOT LIKE, about 98% selectivity, so it is never below threshold) for no regression.
issues.expected_gain: q08 -20..-35% (HJ 0.405s of 0.77s CPU). Also selective-BF lineitem scans in q17 (0.1% pass), q05 (3%), q07, q09, q19, q02, q14. Geomean maybe -3..-6%.
issues.generality: Any scan with a selective filter (pushed predicate, zone-map-surviving range, or join BF/min-max) feeding joins, projections or aggregates. This is very common in star-schema queries. Could be slower: scans at 10-25% selectivity, where the copy cost approaches the saved overhead (hence the low threshold), and LIMIT queries that read slightly more vectors before stopping.
issues.risk: Medium. It touches the core scan path. Pending-chunk carry-over and the CanRemoveFilterColumns projection must be correct. Row-id columns and batch indexes must stay within one parallel range. Order is preserved because coalescing is sequential within one thread's range.
